sources.title: Using approved third-party equipment with Xfinity Internet and Xfinity Voice
sources.evidenceNote: Customer-owned modems, routers, and gateways are allowed when certified and suitable for the member's service; model, speed-tier, address, and Voice compatibility require Xfinity's current device check.

sources.title: Device Info — Xfinity Compatible Modems
sources.evidenceNote: Xfinity's address- and plan-aware database is the final check for current modem recommendations and compatibility.

sources.title: Learn About AT&T Internet Equipment
sources.evidenceNote: AT&T provides the Wi-Fi gateway that connects AT&T Internet or Fiber service to the home.

sources.title: Get Help With DMZ+ Zone Devices
sources.evidenceNote: AT&T documents IP Passthrough for BGW210 and BGW320 gateways, allowing one downstream device to receive the passthrough assignment.

sources.title: Connect your Devices to T-Mobile Internet
sources.evidenceNote: Third-party routers connect to the T-Mobile gateway by Ethernet; supported Wi-Fi 6 mesh/extender products are compatible; the T-Mobile gateway does not offer bridge mode.

sources.title: Authorized Modems to Use on the Spectrum Network
sources.evidenceNote: Spectrum maintains the current authorized-modem list; exact eligibility remains model-, service-, and location-dependent and must be rechecked before purchase or activation.

sources.title: Advanced Wireless Gateway — Spectrum Community
sources.evidenceNote: A verified Spectrum employee states that Spectrum supplies separate modem and router equipment and that a customer router can connect directly to the modem.

sources.title: Using Your Own Modem Device With Cox Internet
sources.evidenceNote: Cox permits customer-owned equipment when the exact modem is certified for the network and selected tier; a separate router is needed when the modem does not include routing or Wi-Fi.

sources.title: Cox Certified Cable Modems
sources.evidenceNote: Cox's current device list is the final model and speed-tier check; unsupported devices are not activated as new or replacement equipment.

sources.title: MoCA to Ethernet Self Install for Fios Internet Speed Upgrade
sources.evidenceNote: Verizon identifies the ONT as the device that converts the fiber signal into separate TV, voice, and data signals and documents the Ethernet handoff used for upgraded internet service.

sources.title: Self-Install Verizon Fios Services
sources.evidenceNote: Fios service depends on an installed ONT whose status and eligibility are verified by Verizon; router setup occurs downstream of that optical termination.

sources.title: Fios Customer Agreement
sources.evidenceNote: The current agreement recognizes routers or extenders purchased from Verizon or a third party and states that Verizon set-top-box streaming requires a compatible Fios router.

sources.title: Fios TV Home App FAQs
sources.evidenceNote: Verizon documents that non-Verizon routers cannot access every Fios TV Home app function and that some multi-router arrangements can block streaming or automatic pairing.

sources.title: What Are Multi-Gig Ethernet and 2.5G Multi-Gig Ethernet Ports?
sources.evidenceNote: NETGEAR documents 1, 2.5, and 5 Gbps multi-gig rates and explains that a gigabit port limits a multi-gig connection to a 1 Gbps Ethernet line rate.
